findings.title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The background cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This makes *every* cleanup job (temp file scanning, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, annotation cleanup, user invites, short URLs, query history row-limit enforcement) run 10x more frequently, multiplying DB and filesystem load on all installations. The `clean()` function also uses a 9-minute timeout, so a long-running cleanup cycle now overlaps with ticks that are simply dropped, making the effective schedule unpredictable. Nothing in the PR description justifies this change; it looks like leftover debugging and should be reverted to 10 minutes (or made configurable deliberately).

findings.title: Debug logging left in at Error level, dumping entire ID batches
findings.body: Six `r.log.Error(...)` calls were added in `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579). These are informational/debug traces, not errors: they fire on every cleanup batch even on full success, and they log the complete `ids` slice, which can contain up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` entries (the test in this PR uses 32767). Consequences: log files and alerting pipelines keyed on ERROR level will be spammed every cleanup cycle (now every minute), with multi-hundred-KB lines. Additionally the `"err", err` field in the pre-delete log statements is always nil, since a non-nil error has already returned. These statements should be removed or downgraded to Debug without the full ID dump.

findings.title: Placeholder-limit workaround keyed on config value and only applied for SQLite
findings.body: `deleteByIDs` decides whether to inline IDs based on `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` and `GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite`, not on `len(ids)` or on the actual driver's limit. Two problems: (1) for non-SQLite backends there is no guard at all, so an operator who sets `annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size` above the backend's bind-parameter limit (65535 for PostgreSQL and MySQL's protocol) will get hard failures from the new `DELETE ... IN (?,?,...)` statement, where the previous sub-query-based DELETE used no parameters at all; (2) the condition is driven by configuration rather than the real number of IDs, so the behaviour is inconsistent with the statement actually being built. Consider chunking `ids` into fixed-size groups (e.g. 999/65535) independently of the configured batch size, for all dialects.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body: The SQLite inline-IDs path builds the value list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside the loop, reallocating and copying the whole accumulated string on each of up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` iterations. With the 32767 batch size exercised by the new test this copies on the order of gigabytes per batch and allocates tens of thousands of intermediate strings, for every cleanup batch. Use a `strings.Builder` (or `strconv.AppendInt` into a byte slice, as `getAccessControlFilter` already does) instead.

findings.title: Per-subtest table cleanup is registered after assertions that can abort the subtest
findings.body: `t.Cleanup` that deletes rows from `annotation`/`annotation_tag` is registered only after `createTestAnnotations`, `assertAnnotationCount` and `assertAnnotationTagCount` have run. Those helpers use `require`, which aborts the subtest immediately on failure; in that case the cleanup is never registered and the inserted rows persist in the shared `fakeSQL` database, causing all following subtests (which assert absolute row counts and insert explicit primary keys) to fail with cascading, misleading errors. Register the cleanup before inserting the fixtures.

findings.title: New subtest inserts 40003 annotations and 80006 tags, making the suite much slower
findings.body: The added "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER" case inserts 40003 annotations plus 80006 annotation_tag rows and then deletes 40000 of them, in a test that also runs against MySQL/Postgres in CI. This is a large fixed cost on every run of the integration suite. The parameter-limit behaviour could be exercised with a far smaller dataset (e.g. batch size just above 999 with a few thousand rows), since the threshold in `deleteByIDs` is 999, not 32767.
